ai.description: *Chikila gaiduwani* is a limbless, earthworm-like amphibian reaching 20–30 cm. It is dark grey to purple-brown with a distinct, protruding snout and recessed, hidden eyes.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Chikila gaiduwani* is best distinguished from other Indian chikilids by its unique, pale-colored, fleshy-white snout tip, which contrasts sharply with its darker body.
ai.habitat: *Chikila gaiduwani* inhabits moist, tropical evergreen forests in Northeast India, typically found burrowing in damp soil at elevations between 800 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: *Chikila gaiduwani* is a burrowing amphibian that exhibits maternal care by brooding its eggs in underground chambers and remaining with them until they hatch.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Chikila gaiduwani* is oviparous and exhibits maternal care, with females guarding clutches of 15–20 eggs in underground burrows during the monsoon breeding season.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Chikila gaiduwani* is endemic to the Garo Hills in the Indian state of Meghalaya, typically found at elevations between 800 and 1,200 meters.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Chikila gaiduwani* consists of a series of short, high-pitched, pulsed chirps emitted by individuals hidden within moist, subterranean soil tunnels.
